newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TISCO wary of political turmoil.
newsitem.headline: India's TISCO wary of political turmoil.

text.p: The chief of India's largest private steelmaker, Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), said on Thursday that political uncertainty in the capital and the eastern state of Bihar threatened to affect the firm's working.
"Factors that will affect the company's working will be political uncertainty in Bihar and Delhi," chairman Ratan Tata told a meeting of shareholders in Bombay.

TISCO's major plants and investments are in the steel city of Jamshedpur in eastern Bihar, which was recently rocked by speculation over the arrest of former Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav in a fodder scandal.
Yadav leads a breakaway faction of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party.

Earlier, Tata had announced a 10 percent rise in sales during the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March), as compared to the corresponding period a year earlier. Exports had risen 23 percent to $42 million year-on-year, he added.
Tata said he believed the political winds would also affect the flow of overseas funds.

"The political uncertainty will also have an impact on foreign inflows and outflows," Tata added. "International prices will have a direct effect on TISCO and infrastructure activities will also have a direct effect on TISCO."
Analysts say that India's economic reforms will grind to a halt unless its crumbling infrastructure sector receives a rapid infusion of funds. Many expect a boom in the sector soon.
Tata said 96/97 has been a difficult year. "The increase in the supply of steel and the downtrend in prices has affected the company, although revenues were up nine percent," he said.
But TISCO remained vibrant, he added.
"The fundamentals of TISCO remain as strong as ever," Tata said in reply to a query.
Holding company Tata Sons also planned to raise its equity in TISCO, Tata added.
"Yes, Tata Sons plans to raise its equity holding in TISCO," he said in reply to a query. "It has always been our endeavbour to increase holdings for all core companies."
But Tata declined to be drawn into speculation over the possibility of a bonus issue of shares.
"The board will act in the manner they deem appropriate," he said.
